text:
sales-anu: Heads up: NimbusHealth POC is glitching during the live walkthrough. They see a lot of slow first-byte TTFT and intermittent 429s when they push multiple patient transcripts. Deal momentum is slipping. Can we triage?

rami: Which model/runtimes? Any recent deploys?

devon: They're using rwd-7b-quant on shared-hosted, batching_strategy=auto, client spawns 20 simultaneous streams (websocket streaming), avg payload ~400 tokens. No recent deploys on our side.

eng-oncall: I'm seeing the thread in logs. Highlights:

```
[2026-03-20T15:07:12Z] request_id=ff7a user=nimbus key=nimbus-poc status=429 reason=per_key_concurrency
[2026-03-20T15:07:14Z] request_id=ff7b user=nimbus model=rwd-7b-quant ttft_ms=2850 cache_hit=false batch_size=10
[2026-03-20T15:07:18Z] request_id=ff7f user=nimbus status=200 ttft_ms=980 cache_hit=true batch_size=4
[2026-03-20T15:07:22Z] request_id=ff82 user=nimbus ttft_ms=3400 cache_miss=true reason=prompt_variation
```

eng-oncall: Cache hit rate only ~22% in the spike. Also seeing several long tails where batch_size jumps to 10-12 before the request executes.

ops-liz: Could be client-side burstiness + our auto-batcher waiting up to latency target to fill the batch. With streaming and high concurrency that interaction can push TTFT up.

rami: Customer app is normalizing user meta inline (patient_id, visit_ts) per prompt which defeats prefix caching. They also send short follow-ups but in separate sessions, so no in-memory KV reuse.

infra-mike: Quick mitigations we can do now:
- limit client concurrency (recommend 6) and enable client-side exponential backoff for 429s
- change batching_strategy=latency_p50 and max_batch_wait_ms=20 so the runtime favors faster dispatching
- add a temporary per-key concurrency bump for nimbus-poc during demo (sales approved?)
- create a cache normalization guide for POC (strip/normalize patient_id before prompt)

eng-oncall: I'll flip the runtime config for the key to bias towards smaller batches and enable debug tracing for 5 minutes to capture latency breakdowns.

sales-anu: Approving quota bump for 1 hour. Please note we need a pricing note if they want sustained reserved capacity.

security-june: Quick reminder: because this is healthcare data, enable prompt_redaction, ensure logs are PII-sanitized, and confirm that retention for this key is set to 0-days for raw prompts if requested.

devon: I pushed a small change to their client template to replace patient_id with patient_hash and grouped small follow-ups into a single request where possible.

eng-oncall: Changes deployed. Initial metrics after 2m:
- 429s: down from 12/min to 1/min
- cache hit rate: up from 22% -> 46%
- median TTFT: 2.9s -> 1.05s
- p95 TTFT improved from 5.2s -> 1.9s

sre-bot: Temporary quota increase applied: per_key_concurrency=8 for key=nimbus-poc for 60m. Routing unchanged.

sales-anu: Great work. Nimbus team is happy and we extended the trial. Next: follow up with a short doc on suggested reserved sizing and a security Q&A about PII handling.

infra-mike: For follow-up I'll run a quick cost delta sim for dedicated pool vs. shared with quota bump and send numbers by EOD.

security-june: I'll prepare a sanitized answer for their security questionnaire and propose an onsite SOC review if they go enterprise.

sales-anu: Thanks everyone, marking this thread resolved unless someone sees regressions.
